rule_level_problems.problem: The check_for has three separate Erythema items: plain, Poorly defined, and Well defined + Raised. The boil rule consumes plain Erythema, while cellulitis and erysipelas need the qualified forms. A clinician who records plain Erythema for a cellulitis patient gets no cellulitis or erysipelas rule. One who records qualified Erythema for a boil may miss the boil rule, depending on whether a qualified finding matches the unqualified one. This is not wrong, but the three overlapping prompts make it easy to record the wrong form.
'Suspected meningitis' in the zoster referral list is not encoded as a possible rule, and Headache and Neck stiffness are not checked for. It is borderline because it sits inside a referral list.

There is no system_priority_evaluation. This is correct, because the red box only cross-references page 82 and lists no criteria of its own. The same-day referral lists stay unencoded as management, by design.

summary: All five 'likely' conclusions on the page (boil/abscess, cellulitis, erysipelas, herpes zoster, hidradenitis suppurativa) are probable rules. Each has the page's criteria ANDed, the hidradenitis sites ORed, and SNOMED concepts that all exist and fit. The red box is only a cross-reference to page 82, so no priority rule is owed. The only gaps are borderline: 'suspected meningitis' and the 'if infected' criteria in the zoster management text are not encoded, and the three overlapping Erythema forms in the check list are a minor recording hazard.
